notes:
**Run a shared project's whole life — from either side.** Admin becomes a real role, the main window stops getting in the way, and Keen's paperwork comes aboard.

## Admin, a real role

- **Add and delete on a shared project** — an Admin can create and delete tasks and milestones in a project shared with them, not just edit what's already there.
- **Descriptions follow the role** — Planners and Admins can edit project and milestone descriptions, and prose editing follows your role instead of being locked to the owner.
- **A share can come back.** Re-accepting a share that was revoked brings the project back whole — with your own tags, notes and reminders still on it — instead of starting over.

## The window is not the app

- **Close the window, not the app.** Closing Keen's main window now hides it: capture windows, reminders and sync keep working, and the Dock icon brings it right back. ⌘Q still quits.
- **Quick capture reaches shared projects.** ⌘N can add a task — and ⇧⌘N a milestone — to a project someone shared with you. If the save is interrupted, trying again won't add it twice.

## Quieter, truer status

- **One globe says how a share is doing** — green when connected, amber while connecting, red when access was revoked. Rows speak up only when something needs attention, and when a share ends for good the item goes quiet instead of staying loud.

## Paperwork on board

- **Acknowledgements** — the open-source components Keen ships are listed in the app menu under Acknowledgements, generated from the actual build.
- **A finished licence agreement** in the installer, and an updated privacy policy at [thekeen.app/privacy](https://thekeen.app/privacy).

---

**Updating:** Keen updates itself — you'll be prompted on next launch, or check Settings → Updates.

**Managed servers:** this release updates the backend too. If you're on a managed server, Keen will ask you to update it after the app restarts; that takes about a minute.
